steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: It's stuck. I can feel its leg...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Pull it out.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Won't it hurt the mother?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: They're stronger than you think.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Alright, I'm pulling!

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Pull!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I wiped its nose and mouth clean. It can breathe now, but it's too weak to stand up and drink from the mother. What should we do?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Ah, okay...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...No, it's still not standing up.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Well, it was born about half a month early, due to today's accident.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Carry it back. We'll have to feed it by hand for a while.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: What if... it never stands up?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Don't make any assumptions about its fate, Jessica. Like I said, they're stronger than you think.

steps.name: Anxious Man
steps.text: Mr. Woodrow! We need you back at camp!

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Anxious Man
steps.text: Th-There's a fight!

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: You go first, Jessica, I need to get the burdenbeasts back into the corral.

steps.name: Anxious Man
steps.text: Jessica? But things are pretty chaotic right now. I'm not sure if she—

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Yeah, I'm not sure if I—

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: It'll be fine. Go. I'll be there right after I take care of these guys.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But what if—

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Just go and see what's going on. You'll need to learn to deal with this stuff on your own sooner or later.

steps.name: Onlookers
steps.text: Do it! Give 'em the ol' one-two!

steps.name: Onlookers
steps.text: Man, that kick must've hurt.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Excuse me, gentlemen, please disperse.

steps.name: Anxious Man
steps.text: B-Be careful, Jessica. These guys ain't the type to look before throwing a punch.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: No need to worry about me. So what happened? Why are they fighting?

steps.name: Anxious Man
steps.text: I-I'm not sure.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: What do I do now...?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Leave it to me, I'll take care of this.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: (The crowd's too thick for me to go in directly...)

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Maybe I can get in from above.
The girl quickly assesses her surroundings. Vehicles and low wooden houses, scattered fencing and scaffolds, and a tall water tower directly in the middle of the camp.
She quickly plots an unobstructed route through the scattered buildings.
She unwinds a rope from one of the tents, climbs one of the scaffolds, and uses the rope to swing to the central water tower.
From there, she has a complete view of the chaotic scene on the ground.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Looks like the brawl began with those two at the center. The rest simply went with the flow.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: So if I stop them, the others should settle down too.
She leaps down and lands in the center of the crowd, lithely dodging an incoming punch before grabbing the attacker's arm and wrestling him to the ground.
Pinning her opponent, she takes a deep breath and shouts—

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: All of you, stop this immediately!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Let's sit down and talk it out.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: We should be helping each other out here on the frontier, not picking fights. We need to learn to accept our differences.

steps.name: Angry Woman
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: Tch...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Ahem... So how did you two start fighting in the first place? You even dragged the rest of the camp into it.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Talk to me. Maybe I can help mediate.

steps.name: Angry Woman
steps.text: Oh, you'll hear me out then?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Angry Woman
steps.text: It all started two months ago...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: (Two months... Their grudge goes back that far? I should have noticed sooner.)

steps.name: Angry Woman
steps.text: We were at the market together, discussing whether to keep fowlbeasts or burdenbeasts once we're married.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Wait... you're getting married?

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: Darn tootin'! If we don't do it now, the baby will have to be born next winter.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: So... you were fighting over whether to get fowlbeasts or burdenbeasts?

steps.name: Angry Man & Woman
steps.text: Yeah!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...Is that really worth coming to blows over?

steps.name: Angry Man & Woman
steps.text: Of course!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'm sorry, I'm still confused... Can you go into more detail?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: (Maybe it's more complicated than that... I should hear them out.)

steps.name: Angry Woman
steps.text: A few fowlbeasts won't make us any money! We should be raising burdenbeasts!

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: And I'm supposed to just leave you alone at camp while I take them out into the wilds to go grazing?!

steps.name: Angry Woman
steps.text: You think I can't take care of myself?!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: No need to stand up, ma'am. Use your words.

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: Who'd worry about a woman who can take out a grown man with a single punch?!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Sir, you should sit down too...

steps.name: Onlookers
steps.text: Stop arguing and settle this the old-fashioned way!

steps.name: Onlookers
steps.text: Fight! Fight! Fight!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Just calm down, everyone... Er, what am I supposed to do here?

steps.name: Angry Woman
steps.text: You're just afraid I'll cheat on you, aren't you?!

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: Where the hell did that come from?!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Folks, please, just sit down...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: (Don't fight anymore, please...)

steps.name: Angry Woman
steps.text: Then what are you on about?!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: (Oh dear...)

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: Obviously it's because...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Er...
Seeing the fire in the couple's eyes, Jessica nervously clenches her fist and readies herself for the coming storm.

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: Because...

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: Because I'd miss you every second I'm away!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Well, well, now ain't that touching.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: But while we're all being honest, there's another score that needs settling: the damages to the camp.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: What do you think, Jessica?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I... I just want to cry right now.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Jessica?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: They were only fighting because they didn't want to be apart... What am I supposed to do about that?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I just... I just...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Wah...

steps.name: Embarrassed Man
steps.text: Hey now, girl, no need to cry... What do we do, honey?

steps.name: Embarrassed Woman
steps.text: Look, we're not fighting anymore. Wipe those tears, okay?

steps.name: Embarrassed Man
steps.text: See? We're holding hands!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: S-Seeing you two make up just makes me want to cry even more...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Here, a towel... Wipe your face.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Sorry, Woody... All I could do was cry...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Just take it nice and easy. There's still plenty you got left to learn.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: I come in, and the first thing I see is Jessica crying. Go easy on the kid, no need to use harsh language.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'm okay, Miles... That's not why... I-It's because...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: It's fine, let it all out. So how's the fence coming along, Miles?

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: Made the mother and child a luxury suite with plenty of straw. The mom eats well, the kid eats well.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Can I go and see the little guy?

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: After dinner. It's already on the table. You're gonna tell us all about your heroic exploits today.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: I heard you swung right into the crowd on a rope and stopped the entire brawl.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I-I learned all that when I was a mercenary. It just felt like the best course of action...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Well, the way I heard it, you sat there crying while they were going at each other's throats, and it freaked them out so much they dropped everything to cheer you up.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: No wonder your eyes were so red. So that's your secret weapon.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I-I'm sorry, I couldn't control my emotions.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: They kept arguing over whether to buy fowlbeasts or burdenbeasts, and I didn't even know what to say... I could barely understand what they were talking about.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Maybe I could have stopped them sooner if I did.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: It's not like you've ever had the chance to learn this stuff. You're overthinking it. Next time there's something like that, just...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Just what?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Easy. Take out your gun and shoot it into the sky. That'll get their attention, I guarantee it.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: Ain't that what you used to do in the restaurant back in the day, Woody?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Who else would I be talking about?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Well, it don't matter how you do it, as long as it gets the job done.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: What did you tell those people, anyway? They paid for the damages and dispersed without a word of complaint.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I told 'em they had a choice: behave themselves and stay in camp, or get out and fend for themselves in the wilderness.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I-Isn't that a little extreme?

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: Little ruckuses like that can get real messy if you get bogged down in the details. Woody has the right of it. Cut straight to the heart of the matter.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I see... I've never dealt with a situation like that.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Maybe I should try Woody's method.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: But remember, you're not me. Don't go overthinking this.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...Yeah, I don't have half the experience that you do.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: That's not what I— Never mind.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Alright, no long faces at the dinner table. Help me set the table, Jessica.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Okay... one, two, three, four, five... there's one set too many.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Helena, I put the extra set back.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: That can't be right, I was sure I counted it out. There are five of us, so...

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: (Turns to the side)

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Helena, I...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Old habits die hard, don't they...? Let's eat.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Come on, stand up little guy...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Woody is taking the herd out to the wilds next month. You won't be able to keep up like this.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Jessica? It's getting dark. You should come back.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Coming.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: That's what you said last time, and I didn't see you back until sunrise.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Is Helena asleep? I didn't realize... I thought she just made a mistake. I shouldn't have reminded her.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Still bothered by what happened at the dinner table?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: She's been so kind to me ever since I arrived. But I was inconsiderate of her feelings...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I should know just how much of a blow the loss of Mr. Leone was to everyone... Better than anyone.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Just come in. She's fine. It's not your fault.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Are you really going next month, Woody?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Yeah, the seasons wait for no one.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But there's so much I still need to learn...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: It's just for two months. Everyone's here to help.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But I didn't even notice the feelings of those close to me... How am I supposed to take care of the entire camp?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: If that's what you're worried about, I'll teach you more before leaving. But get ready, 'cause you'll have even more responsibilities going forward.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: That's fine with me... But you're already so busy every day.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: At my age, losing a few hours of sleep ain't no big deal.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Woody...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: If you have something to say, say it.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: You say you don't sleep much... but I didn't expect you to be up so early.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Well, here's the bad news: you'll have to be up at the same time once I'm gone. Make the rounds, turn off the lights, maintenance check... You'll have your hands full with all the little things going on at camp.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Can I... really manage?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Depends on how well you do this month. You haven't touched that gun of yours since you quit the mercenary life. Not rusty, are you?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I... practice in the forest every day.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Fighting out here is very different from what you're used to at Blacksteel. Your old methods won't work, and you won't have access to the same equipment and support.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: How do you do it, then?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Look ahead.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: It's dark... I can't see anything.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Look closer.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: That's...
She squints, trying to see into the dark swamp.
Suddenly, she sees a little glint.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...Glass.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Some ampule bottles I got from a wandering doctor. See if you can hit them.
She raises her gun, struggling to zero-in on the ephemeral speck of light.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Good. Now the one further away.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Alright...
Gunshots, then the sound of breaking glass. Soon, there is only one last speck of light in the distance, almost impossible to see.
The girl holds her breath and prepares to fire the last shot.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Jessica...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Are you really worried that you won't be able to do your job properly?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: If there's something you want to say, Woody, just say it.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I can't say this for 100% certain, but looking at you these past few days, I get the feeling that what you're really worried about is that you won't fit in.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: This is a very different environment from what you're used to. It's normal to have growing pains.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: For the past few months, you've been trying to act like an experienced Pioneer around the others in camp, and like an old friend around us old folks.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: But it's only been half a year since you came. Half a year since you met us.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Am I not expected to grow up quickly and fit in?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Growing up means becoming a better person, not a different one.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Life ain't a jigsaw puzzle. Fitting in ain't about filling the gap someone else left behind.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I don't think that's fair to me. You've seen everything I've accomplished so far.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: ...Then hit the last bottle.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Woody... You shouldn't jump to conclusions.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Let's finish the exercise first.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Woody...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Alright... We'll do it your way.
She once again takes aim at the bottle, but her shots keep missing.
Suddenly, her pupil contracts, capturing the tiny speck of reflection from the bottle.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: You missed.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: It was just one miss. I'll hit it next time.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Deep down, you know I'm right. The targets were set up to match your skill level. You should've been able to hit all of them.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: But you didn't.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Are you saying your words distracted me?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Do you deny it?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I'm worried, Jessica. Is your stubborn refusal to face your discomfort a sign of strength, or are you just embarrassed to admit that coming out to the frontier was a mistake?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Maybe you ain't really prepared to live out here. Maybe you just didn't want to stay at Blacksteel.
The old man takes out a coin and tosses it into the air. It lands on the back of his hand, and he covers it with his other hand.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: What are you doing?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Couldn't make up my mind. My heart wants you to stay, but my mind tells me you should go back to your family. So I'll leave the decision to fate.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Heads or tails?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: And if I guess right?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Then you can stay. But if you guess wrong, I'll have someone take you home.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: This is ridiculous. You have no right to make that decision for me.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: It ain't me. It's the coin.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...It makes no difference, Woody.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Make a choice. You know me. I say something, I mean it.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Alright...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: You're right, Woody. I felt frustrated.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I admit it. I wasn't ready. Life on the frontier is strange and unfamiliar.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Caring for burdenbeasts, fixing fences, raising foals... it's all new to me. All the skills I learned at Blacksteel mean nothing here.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Do you regret it, Jessica?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: No. I don't regret it, and I'm not leaving, whether that coin comes up heads or tails.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: No one is ever completely ready. The only thing I can do is tell myself not to be afraid, whatever comes.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I made a choice, and I intend to take responsibility. If I choose to stay, I'll stay. I won't let a stupid coin make my decision for me.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: And I...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I want to stay with you guys.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Just because your grandpa left you doesn't mean you have to find someone else to fill the void.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'm sorry...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Jessica, you bonehead.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Woody...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: This is no stupid coin.
The old man raises his arm, revealing the object on the back of his hand.
It is flat, round and solid, with a star etched in the center, gleaming in the morning light.
In Columbia, Pioneers give it to someone worthy of trust. Someone who will protect the camp from trouble and threats.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Th-This is your sheriff badge.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: It's yours now. You think you're not ready. I think you are.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: The only preparation you need to face the future is to not be afraid of it.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: C'mere. I'll pin it on for you.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...Am I really ready to wear this?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Of course. You're willing to cry for a stranger. That means you're willing to fight for 'em.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I knew it the moment I saw you.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...I promise. I'll take care of everyone while you're away.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I mean it.
She touches the badge on her chest, then suddenly hears a bellowing from the forest. The duo turn around and look towards the sound.
A herd of burdenbeasts emerges from the forest. At the rear is a tiny foal, its steps unsteady yet determined.
